title: Teaching her sons and shifting from Dixieland to modern styles
summary: She moved from Dixieland, ragtime and swing with her brothers to modern music with her sons, taught them fundamentals; Gerald picked up bass in a day.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: I enjoyed hearing your band the other night.

Most of them is three-part rags. And now I came back. Let's get back to the time of music. I played the Dixieland, the rake time, the swing with my brothers. And then after we got to the boys, well, I had to go in a more modern direction.
Yes, of course. Music keeps changing like everything else.
Then I had to change to modern. So we all, me and the outfit, we are versatile. We play every type of music. I taught the boys the Dixieland music, you see.
Did you teach them most of their music, too, on the different instruments?
Well, I only had to teach them the fundamentals of music.
Yes, and the reading and the time.

They picked it up right now. And Justin took lessons from Professor Mineta, for the guitar. Where is it? The guitar. The drummer, Pussy. He just picked it up. Didn't have to teach them. No more than the fundamentals. Yes.
There's a lot of children that way, especially here in New Orleans, where they've heard all of this music all their life and have that background. A lot of them do it with very, very special.
Gerald bought a bass on a Wednesday and played his first job on Thursday. Oh, really?
And he played a little bit on the piano or anything else?
I guess he knew a little bit about music. He used to play a little bit on the piano.
He knew a little music already.
And he just worked all night with the bass. All day and all night. And all the next day until it was time for the job. And he played the job.
Did he get to rehearse with him before in the band? No, no, no. Just went right on to play?
No, he just went right to it.
How old was he when he did that? Sixteen. Sixteen? Mm-hmm. Very good.
And Gerald is still a very good piano player, too. Mm-hmm.
You still practice on the instrument or you just wait until you work someplace?
No, we don't all. We don't ever practice.
You don't? No. No. No.
Justin, this is the oldest one. That's a guitar player. He plays along with, around with, right now he's playing with a modern band, you know, a rock and roll band, but he's played with Dixon.
